![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14093452/assets/c6556825089b3b475615ed4a8ebf9eff2e6db3d76eb26103312f736a3e114793.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the path along the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{8},$ shown above?
worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to arc length over $C$ is equal to the arc length $L$ of $C,$ i.e.,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.
$$

In polar coordinates, the arc length element $\text{d}s$ is given by

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

So, for a polar curve defined as $r=r(\theta )$ for ${\theta }_{1}\le \theta \le {\theta }_{2},$ we have

$$
L={\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-8\operatorname{sin}⁡4\theta .
$$

Therefore, the expression for our line integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta )}^{2}+{(-8\operatorname{sin}⁡4\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡4\theta +64{sin}^{2}⁡4\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡4\theta +4{sin}^{2}⁡4\theta +60{sin}^{2}⁡4\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{4+60{sin}^{2}⁡4\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{1+15{sin}^{2}⁡4\theta }\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
